title: Mind-only clear perception — intelligentia vs scientia
source_text: VII. Alias vero objectum sensus ipsos non ferit, sed menti tantum sese offert, & clare ac distincte ab ea percipitur. Idque adhuc bifariam. Vel enim res proposita immediate, sive propria & innata luce, sine ullo discursu & ratiocinio, mentem movet ad assensum. Quo pacto percipimus veritatem principiorum, & eorum quae sunt per se nota. Quale est, idem simul non potest esse & non esse, bis duo sunt quatuor, si aequalibus aequalia addas tota erunt aequalia, & quae sunt ejusmodi. Et haec certitudo potest ad distinctionem dici certitudo intelligentiae. Vel res, quae menti judicanda offertur, propria quidem luce mentem ita non ferit, sed intellectus discurrendo & ratiocinando ex principiis per se notis colligit & judicat omnino & simpliciter impossibile esse ut res aliter se habeat. Quomodo mens percipit veritatem conclusionum, quas ex primis principiis evidenter deducit, & quas propterea dici potest videre luce quadam ex illis reflexa. Et haec certitudo dicitur certitudo scientiae.
pass_a_gloss: But otherwise the object does not strike the senses themselves, but only offers itself to the mind, and is clearly and distinctly perceived by it. And that still in two ways. For either the proposed thing immediately, by its own and innate light, without any discourse and reasoning, moves the mind to assent. In which manner we perceive the truth of principles and of things known through themselves. Such as: the same thing cannot at once be and not be; twice two are four; if you add equals to equals the wholes will be equal; and things of that kind. And this certainty can by way of distinction be called the certainty of intelligence. Or the thing offered to the mind for judging does not so strike the mind by its own light, but the intellect by discoursing and reasoning from principles known through themselves gathers and judges that it is altogether and simply impossible that the thing be otherwise. In which manner the mind perceives the truth of conclusions which it evidently deduces from first principles, and which therefore it can be said to see by a certain light reflected from them. And this certainty is called the certainty of science.
pass_b_english: Object to mind only (not outer sense) — still clear/distinct.
Immediate innate light → principles / per se nota = certitudo intelligentiae.
Discursive light from principles → conclusions = certitudo scientiae.

choices.english: this certainty is called the certainty of science
